the maintenance of receptor clusters and caveola membrane specializations depends upon the presence and availability of cholesterol in the plasma membrane.

cholesterol plays a role in maintaining the clustering of the folate receptor, and that this clustering is dependent on the presence of the phospholipid anchor of the folate binding protein.

the molecular basis of membrane protein targeting and the role of cholesterol in membrane organization.
the role of cholesterol in membrane protein sorting and trafficking.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate the delivery of folate to mammalian cells and with the role of cholesterol in the maintenance of membrane domain structure.

the cholesterol content of the membrane is a major determinant of the clustering and distribution of a GPI-anchored receptor.
the cholesterol-dependent clustering of folate receptor and other GPI-anchored proteins in caveolae may be a general mechanism for the sorting of these receptors into the endocytic pathway.

cholesterol is required for the clustering of folate receptor in MA104 cells and the formation of caveolae.
the cholesterol content of the membrane regulates the clustering of a GPI-anchored protein, the folate receptor, in a caveola.

cholesterol is required for the clustering of the folate receptor and for the maintenance of caveolae.
